labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

ChatGPT Desktop v26.924.22138

### What subscription do you have?

Plus

### What platform is your computer?

macOS

### What issue are you seeing?

[macOS] Window manager creates an off-screen "detached" launcher window with a ghost frame; title-bar hit-test desyncs (traffic lights only clickable in top ~39px strip)

**App:** ChatGPT for macOS v26.924.22138 (Codex Framework 154.0.8037.57)
**OS:** macOS 26.7 Tahoe (25G229), MacBook Pro built-in display ONLY (1800x1169 pts, 3024x1964 Retina)
**Onset:** 2026-09-28, first launch after 14:40 auto-update (following a 14:57 reboot to a single display)
**/feedback session ID:** `no-active-thread-01a0ea4c-5681-7a63-ab70-41022ceb9008`

## Symptoms

1. **Title-bar hit-test desync (always reproducible):** with the main window restored (not maximized), the traffic-light buttons only respond to clicks in a **~39 px-tall strip at the very top**; the rest of the button area is dead. **Maximizing the window fixes it** (buttons clickable across their full area).
2. **Hide-away choreography (with Pets enabled):** after opening, the main window self-maximizes (~1 s), then **at ~10 s it animates itself off-screen** (measured x=-1364), and **at ~14 s it reappears** at a ghost frame from a previous display configuration (1128x2229 at y=-390/-55; height ~2x the display).
3. **Accessibility tree empty:** System Events returns "Can't get window 1 of process ChatGPT" while windows are visibly on screen (blocks AX users and automation).

## Root evidence

**External measurement (CGWindowList live sampling):** a persistent **off-screen window 1128x2229 at (993,-55), layer 3** coexists with the visible primary window (1800x1068 at 0,39). 1128x2229 matches a stale, unscaled frame from a pre-reboot display configuration.

**The app's own logs confirm the architecture** (`~/Library/Logs/com.openai.codex/2026/09/28/`):
```
[window-manager] window main frame finished load appearance=primary       windowId=1
[window-manager] window ready-to-show           appearance=detached       windowId=2   <- ~7 s later
[window-manager] window main frame finished load appearance=avatarOverlay windowId=3
```
Each launch creates **three** windows. The `detached` one (windowId=2) is the off-screen ghost-frame carrier; the title-bar hit-test offset matches the **detached** window's coordinates, not the visible primary's.

## Pets A/B

- **Show pet enabled:** reproduces fully (hide-away choreography + ghost frame + empty AX tree).
- **Pets disabled + persisted pet state removed** (`electron-avatar-overlay-open`, `electron-avatar-overlay-bounds` incl. orphaned `displayId` 2/5 and `byResolution` entries in `~/.codex/.codex-global-state.json`): hide-away stops (main window stable 30+ min), **but the hit-test offset still reproduces** -> the defect lives in the window-manager layer, not in Pets persistence itself.
- **Falsification experiment:** with the app closed, wrote a correct overlay frame (1650,1000, display 1, no orphan displays) into the daemon state; on relaunch the app **ignored it** and recreated the corrupt 1128x2229 frame -> the bad frame is generated internally (likely cached/unscaled display coords), not read from persisted state.
- **Mini mode:** pending confirmation (per docs, Mini keeps floating controls without the pet — will test whether the offset persists).

**Ruled out:** TCC/permissions (no folder grants; drag & drop is handled by Finder), third-party event taps / window managers (none running at first occurrence), stale daemon state alone (purging fixes the hidden window but not the hit-test).

## Workaround

Keep the main window **maximized**.

## Attachments

- `openai-bug-logs-20260928-REDACTED.zip` — 48 log files, all 2026-09-28 sessions 14:40-16:53 (username redacted to USER). Sensitive-info review done: no emails, no tokens/keys, no IPs.
- Help-center thread and community forum thread (with CGWindowList measurements and A/B details): https://community.openai.com/t/bug-in-macos-desktop-app-gui/1401758

## Request

Review the `detached` launcher window's frame handling after display-configuration changes on single-display Macs (orphaned per-`displayId`/`byResolution` placement), and the title-bar hit-test <-> content desync in restored windows.

Happy to run further repros: fresh user account, disabling the Codex app-server daemon, specific Pets modes (Mini), external-display plug/unplug cycles.


### What steps can reproduce the bug?

### Steps to reproduce

1. On macOS 26.7 Tahoe, let ChatGPT for macOS auto-update to **26.924.22138** and restart the Mac so only the built-in display remains (single display, 1800x1169 pts).
2. Launch ChatGPT and **restore** the main window (un-maximize it).
3. Click the traffic-light buttons (close/minimize/maximize): they only respond in the top ~39 px strip of the button area. Maximizing the window fixes the hit-test until you restore again.
4. (With Pets > Show pet enabled) Observe the window self-maximize at ~1 s, animate itself off-screen at ~10 s (measured x=-1364), and reappear at ~14 s in a ghost frame (1128x2229 at y=-390/-55).
5. While it happens, run this probe (external confirmation of the ghost window):

```bash
swift -e 'import CoreGraphics; import Foundation
if let list = CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo(CGWindowListOption(arrayLiteral: .optionAll), kCGNullWindowID) as? [[String: Any]] {
  for w in list where (w["kCGWindowOwnerName"] as? String) == "ChatGPT" {
    let b = w["kCGWindowBounds"] as? [String: NSNumber] ?? [:]
    print((w["kCGWindowIsOnscreen"] as? NSNumber)?.boolValue ?? false,
          b["X"]?.intValue ?? -99, b["Y"]?.intValue ?? -99,
          b["Width"]?.intValue ?? -99, "x", b["Height"]?.intValue ?? -99,
          "layer", w["kCGWindowLayer"] ?? "?")
  }
}'
```

### What is the expected behavior?

Expected output shows a persistent off-screen `1128x2229` window at `(993,-55) layer 3` (~2x the display height) next to the visible `1800x1068` primary.

The app's own logs (`~/Library/Logs/com.openai.codex/2026/09/28/`) show THREE windows per launch:
```
[window-manager] window main frame finished load appearance=primary       windowId=1
[window-manager] window ready-to-show           appearance=detached       windowId=2
[window-manager] window main frame finished load appearance=avatarOverlay windowId=3
```

### Additional information

**Session IDs:** /feedback `no-active-thread-01a0ea4c-5681-7a63-ab70-41022ceb9008`; desktop log sessions `13835424-63f4-4825-b6bd-83ca1e510ea0` (14:40, onset), `30f295e4-09da-452d-a417-c8baee65a445` (hit-test repro), `0adae6e6-bd9c-4256-85d5-9d0f4f8d8f17` (16:00 falsification experiment), `0ecce31d-267f-44cf-87e9-c956661cb3ea` (pet disabled, offset persists).
**Token limit / context window usage:** not applicable — this is a window-management bug, not a model/context issue.

items.title: Reuse the HTTP connection pool for remote plugin requests
items.body:
Reuse the HTTP connection pool for remote plugin requests

## Why

Each call to `PluginsConfigInput::remote_plugin_service_config` created a new HTTP client pool, preventing connection reuse across service configurations.

## What changed

Share one lazily initialized, route-aware pool across a `PluginsConfigInput` and its clones. Newly constructed inputs retain separate pools, while service configurations continue to use the current endpoint and product SKU and requests use the supplied authentication.

## Testing

Add tests for lazy initialization, pool sharing across repeated calls and early clones, isolation between new inputs, and requests using updated endpoints, product SKUs, and authentication with the shared pool.

items.title: Cache parsed plugin manifests across plugin workflows
items.body:
Cache parsed plugin manifests across plugin workflows

## Why

Repeated plugin discovery and loading reparse unchanged manifests and repeat warnings for invalid fields.

## What changed

- Share a manifest cache through `PluginStore` across marketplace listing, plugin loading, capability inspection, and tool suggestion metadata.
- Reuse successful parses by plugin root, manifest path, and content digests, including the Codex overlay. Reread files on each load so manifest edits and overlay changes or removal remain visible.
- Bound the cache to 128 entries and bypass caching for inputs larger than 64 KiB. Retry failed parses and share entries across store clones while keeping independent stores isolated.
- Reuse loaded manifest data when loading apps and MCP metadata.

## Testing

Add unit coverage for parse reuse, warning deduplication, revision invalidation, repair after parse failures, equivalent Windows paths, store isolation, and oversized inputs. Add an app-server regression test that verifies repeated `plugin/list` requests observe manifest and overlay revisions in one running server.

items.title: Resolve Windows sandbox PowerShell fallbacks on the exec server
items.body:
Resolve Windows sandbox PowerShell fallbacks on the exec server

## Why

Remote controllers cannot resolve a sandbox-compatible PowerShell executable on the execution host.

## What changed

Apply the existing PowerShell fallback during exec-server request preparation for the `Elevated` and `Mxc` Windows sandbox backends. Match `pwsh` and `powershell` executable names case-insensitively and replace inaccessible Store PowerShell paths when a compatible executable is available.

## Testing

Add Windows RPC regression tests for lowercase and mixed-case PowerShell aliases with a restricted server `PATH`, verifying successful command execution in the `Mxc` sandbox.

items.title: Notify lifecycle extensions of compaction usage limits
items.body:
Notify lifecycle extensions of compaction usage limits

## Why

Usage-limit failures during manual or post-turn compaction did not notify turn lifecycle extensions, leaving them unable to react to these errors.

## What changed

Emit the turn error lifecycle notification for `UsageLimitExceeded` in both compaction paths. Preserve the completed answer after post-turn compaction fails, and avoid duplicating the error already emitted by manual compaction.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From "About Codex" dialog)?

Codex Desktop on Windows, MSIX package `OpenAI.Codex_26.924.2738.0_x64` (bundled `codex-cli 0.156.1`).

### What subscription do you have?

Not verified from inside the session. The session runs the built-in `openai` model provider with a custom model slug supplied through `model_catalog_json`.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 x64, PowerShell 7.

### What issue are you seeing?

Tool calls to declared, schema-visible tools are intermittently rejected by the Codex tool dispatcher with the literal error:

```
unsupported call: <tool_name>
```

Affected tools observed in a single session include both connector/MCP-backed tools and the built-in web search tool:

- `web.run` (built-in web search)
- `mcp__codex_apps__github___search_issues`, `mcp__codex_apps__github___get_profile` (GitHub connector)
- `mcp__codex_app__check_app_update`, `mcp__codex_app__list_projects`
- `mcp__ghidra__list_instances`

The tool schemas are present in the session's model-visible tool list, so this is not a "tool never exposed" case. The model emits a call for a tool the session advertised, and the dispatcher rejects it. Local `functions.*` tools (`exec_command`, `apply_patch`) keep working in the same session at the same time.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Configure a custom model through `model_catalog_json` and start a Codex Desktop session on it.
2. Call any connector-backed tool, for example a GitHub connector search, or the built-in web search tool.
3. Observe `unsupported call: <tool_name>`. Retrying the identical call sometimes succeeds and sometimes fails.

### Observed intermittency (single session, in order)

1. One batch of three GitHub connector calls (`get_repo`, `search_issues` x2) succeeded normally.
2. Immediately afterwards, every connector call in the same session was rejected: `search_issues` (x4), `get_profile` (x2), `check_app_update`, `list_projects`, `list_instances`.
3. Earlier, `web.run` succeeded on its first attempt; a few minutes later the identical call failed twice and then succeeded; in the following turn it failed on 8 consecutive attempts.
4. The `web.run` failures are independent of arguments: a single query, a four-query batch, `response_length` set to short/medium/long/omitted, and even an empty query `{"q": ""}` all returned the identical `unsupported call: run`.

### Environment (sanitized)

```toml
# %USERPROFILE%\.codex\config.toml (relevant lines only)
model = "commandcode-goat/deepseek-v4.1-flash"
model_provider = "openai"
model_catalog_json = "%USERPROFILE%\\.codex\\token-model-catalog.json"
standalone_web_search = true
```

The custom catalog entry for this model sets `"supports_search_tool": false` and `"shell_type": "shell_command"`, and has no `tool_mode` field.

### What is the expected behavior?

A tool call whose name matches a declared session tool should either dispatch normally or fail with a precise capability or authorization error. The dispatcher should not intermittently answer `unsupported call` for tools that the session advertised to the model.

### Additional information

- This looks adjacent to, but distinct from, the existing custom-provider MCP reports (#22970, #31354, #26977, #44984, #36382, #47839). Those describe tools that are never exposed, or a provider-specific namespace/deferred-loading problem. Here the schemas are visible, plain local tools keep working, and the same connector call alternates between success and `unsupported call` within one running session.
- An exhaustive duplicate search was not completed because the GitHub connector itself is affected by this bug; its search calls are rejected intermittently.

Reproduction steps
1. Sign into the Linux desktop app and ChatGPT Web/iOS using the same account and workspace.
2. Create a normal Chat conversation in the Linux app.
3. Send a message and receive a response.
4. Confirm the conversation appears in Linux Recents.
5. Check ChatGPT Web and iOS.
6. The Linux-created conversation does not appear.
7. Create a conversation on Web or iOS.
8. That conversation does appear in the Linux app.
Troubleshooting already performed
- Completely quit and restarted the Linux app.
- Verified these are ordinary Chat conversations, not Temporary Chat or Work sessions.
- Removed the existing ~/.config/Codex profile and allowed the application to create a fresh profile.
- Signed in again with fresh authentication.
- Confirmed existing cloud history repopulated successfully.
- Reproduced the Linux → cloud sync failure with the fresh profile.
- Tested explicitly under XWayland:
  chatgpt --ozone-platform=x11
  Result: new Linux chat did not sync.
- Tested explicitly under native Wayland:
  chatgpt --ozone-platform=wayland
  Result: new Linux chat did not sync.
- Verified CODEX_HOME is unset.
- ~/.codex/sessions and ~/.codex/archived_sessions contained no session transcript files.
- The in-app / feedback flow did not provide a session ID.
- Verified package is current:
  Installed: 26.924.50649
  Candidate: 26.924.50649
- No proxy environment variables are set:
  http_proxy, https_proxy, all_proxy, and no_proxy are unset.
- https://ws.chatgpt.com is reachable.
- A generic WebSocket upgrade attempt to wss://ws.chatgpt.com/ reaches the server and returns HTTP 404, as expected for an unauthenticated/non-public root WebSocket endpoint.
- No relevant entries were emitted by:
  journalctl --user -S "10 minutes ago" | grep -i -E "chatgpt|codex|openai"
  or
  sudo journalctl -S "10 minutes ago" | grep -i -E "chatgpt|codex|openai"

ChatGPT Web in Brave on the same Pop!_OS machine and same network syncs normally to iOS.
Likewise, conversations created on iOS sync normally to both Web and the Linux desktop app.
This appears isolated specifically to Linux-desktop-created Chat conversations not being committed to cloud history.
Additional notes
Pop!_OS is not currently listed as an officially supported Linux distribution, although it is Ubuntu 24.04 based.
OpenAI Support directed me to file this issue here after the normal diagnostic steps did not expose a session ID, local session transcript, journal error, or obvious network problem.
I can provide additional targeted diagnostics if needed.

### What issue are you seeing?

There appears to be an account-specific Codex model entitlement discrepancy within the same ChatGPT Business workspace.

- GPT-5.6 Luna
- GPT-5.5

The affected account:

- was originally created in 2022;
- was later migrated from a Personal workspace to Business in 2026;
- has a Business Premium 5x seat;
- is an Owner/Admin of the Business workspace;
- is signed into Codex using ChatGPT authentication, not an API key;
- has been fully logged out of and back into Codex without any change to the available model list.

A legacy-account migration or stale entitlement state is one possible explanation, but I cannot confirm that this is the root cause. The reproducible problem is that two users in the same Business workspace, using the same Codex client/version, receive different model entitlements.

OpenAI Support has so far inferred that this may be rollout/eligibility related, but has not provided an account-specific backend entitlement finding.

There is also a potentially related workspace provisioning inconsistency:

- **Daybreak Blue** is shown as **Active**;

- links presented by the Daybreak UI for managing defaults/models return a 404;
- this prevents the expected Daybreak/model access configuration from being performed.

This may indicate an incomplete account/workspace migration, stale entitlement state, or inconsistent provisioning between Codex model access and newer workspace model-management controls.

Please investigate the affected account's effective Codex model entitlement and determine why it differs from another Business Premium user in the same workspace.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use Codex for Windows version **26.924.22138**.
2. Sign into the affected account using ChatGPT authentication.
3. Select the Business workspace.
4. Open the Codex model picker.
5. Observe that only the following models are available:
   - GPT-5.6 Sol
   - GPT-5.6 Terra
   - GPT-5.6 Luna
   - GPT-5.5
6. Fully sign out of Codex.
7. Sign into the comparison account, which is a member of the same Business workspace.
8. Select the same Business workspace.
9. Open the Codex model picker.
10. Observe that the comparison account additionally has:
    - GPT-6 Sol
    - GPT-6 Astra
    - GPT-6 Luna
11. Sign back into the affected account.
12. Confirm that GPT-6 models remain unavailable.

The discrepancy persists after logging out and back in.

Codex Feedback ID:

**no-active-thread-01a0ea1a-b957-7372-a27a-723ce597f68e**

Existing OpenAI Support case:

**15977381**

### What is the expected behavior?

Users with equivalent Business Premium entitlement and model permissions in the same Business workspace should receive the same eligible Codex model set, unless there is a documented account-specific restriction.

If GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6 Luna are enabled for the workspace and are available to another user in that same workspace, the affected account should also receive those models when its seat, role and permissions are equivalent.

If there is an account-specific eligibility restriction, Codex or the Admin Console should expose the effective entitlement state or reason rather than silently presenting a different model list.

### Additional information

Affected account:

- ChatGPT account originally created in 2022
- Migrated from Personal to Business in 2026
- Business Premium 5x seat
- Owner/Admin
- ChatGPT-authenticated Codex session
- No API key involved
- GPT-6 is available to the affected account in ChatGPT Web, but not in Codex

Comparison account:

- Member of the same Business workspace
- Same Codex Windows client/version
- GPT-6 Sol available
- GPT-6 Astra available
- GPT-6 Luna available

Workspace / admin observations:

- Organisation is Business Verified
- Daybreak Blue is Active
- Organisation is shown as enabled for Daybreak Blue
- Models / Model Test controls are not available in the workspace admin UI
- Models / Model Test controls are not available in the global Admin Console
- Daybreak-provided admin links for model/default management return 404
- OpenAI Support has stated that workspace settings cannot make an unavailable Codex model appear

The strongest reproducible evidence is therefore:

**same Business workspace + same Codex version + different user identity = different Codex model availability**

This appears to be an account-specific entitlement/provisioning inconsistency rather than a normal client-side issue.

items.title: Android app: threads assigned to Sections are inaccessible; Sections only partially work in Remote

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
### What platform/client are you using?

- ChatGPT Android app: 1.2026.265
- Android 17
- Device: Pixel 10
- ChatGPT Plus
- Codex Desktop on Windows is the primary client where Sections are managed

### What issue are you seeing?

Threads assigned to custom Sections in Codex Desktop are not accessible from the normal Android app because the normal Android interface does not show those Sections at all.

This is the primary issue.

There is also a secondary problem in **Remote** inside the Android app:
- custom Sections are visible there,
- but their contents are incomplete,
- i.e. some threads assigned to a Section on desktop appear in Android Remote, while other threads assigned to the same Section do not.

Desktop itself shows the Sections and their thread membership normally.

### Expected behavior

The Android app should expose the same custom Sections and the threads assigned to them, without requiring the user to enter Remote.

Threads should not effectively disappear from normal Android access merely because they were organized into a Section on desktop.

Remote should also show complete Section membership.

### Actual behavior

#### Normal Android app
- Custom Sections are not visible.
- Threads assigned to those Sections are therefore not accessible through the normal Android thread UI.

#### Android Remote
- The Sections themselves are visible.
- Thread membership is incomplete: some Section threads appear, others are missing.

#### Desktop
- Sections and their assigned threads are visible and usable as expected.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In Codex Desktop, start with a thread that is accessible on Android.
2. Move that thread into a custom Section.
3. Open the normal ChatGPT/Codex Android interface.
4. Observe that the Section is not exposed there and the thread is no longer normally accessible.
5. Open Remote in the Android app.
6. Observe that the Section may appear there, but not all threads assigned to it are necessarily listed.
7. Compare against desktop, where the Section and its full membership are visible.

### Why this matters

Sections are intended to organize active Codex threads. If Android does not expose them, organizing threads on desktop can make those threads effectively unavailable on mobile unless Remote happens to surface them.

Remote is not an adequate substitute for normal Android access, and even there the Section membership currently appears incomplete.

### Related but distinct issues

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

ChatGPT Web / Work & Codex (cross-surface request). I am a ChatGPT Plus subscriber.

### What feature would you like to see?

I would like ChatGPT/Codex to offer an **optional, user-authorised usage-awareness capability** that lets the AI take the user's actual remaining Work/Codex capacity into account when recommending how a task should be handled.

Today, a user can inspect usage manually, but the AI helping decide whether a task should remain in ordinary Chat, use a higher reasoning level, or move into Work/Codex does not have access to the same relevant capacity information.

With explicit user permission, the AI should be able to read relevant usage state such as:

- remaining 5-hour and weekly Work/Codex allowance;
- reset timing;
- purchased-credit balance where applicable;
- current model/reasoning/speed cost characteristics; and
- other relevant plan limits that affect execution choice.

It could then make recommendations such as:

- keep this task in ordinary Chat;
- use Work/Codex because the task is sufficiently bounded and substantial;
- Medium reasoning is likely sufficient;
- High reasoning is warranted here;
- remaining capacity is low, so defer or use a cheaper execution path unless the task is high priority.

The capability should be **advisory by default**.

Any stronger authority — for example allowing the AI to choose the execution mode, reasoning level, or initiate Work automatically — should exist only when the user has explicitly delegated that authority, within user-controlled and revocable limits.

The principle is **informed delegation, not autonomous control of the user's allowance**.

### Why this matters

Deciding how to allocate Chat versus Work/Codex is itself a resource-management problem.

The AI can assess task complexity, but without visibility into current allowance it is missing one of the most important variables needed to give a sensible recommendation. The human user therefore has to act as the bridge between two pieces of information that the system already possesses separately:

1. what the task appears to require; and
2. what execution capacity remains.

This becomes particularly important on Plus, where a substantial Work/Codex task or an unnecessarily high reasoning level can consume a meaningful portion of the available allowance.

The desired workflow is not for the AI to take control away from the user. It is for the user to be able to say, in effect:

> You may read my relevant usage state and use it when advising me how to allocate Chat, reasoning effort, and Work/Codex execution.

### Existing capability / precedent

OpenAI Support pointed me to **Personal Analytics** as the closest existing capability. As currently documented, that is a read-only analytics capability available only to eligible Enterprise/Edu workspaces rather than individual Plus subscribers.

That suggests much of the underlying read-only usage-analysis concept already exists. This request is to make the relevant usage-awareness available to individual subscribers and usable by the assistant when making execution recommendations.

### Relationship to existing requests

I searched existing issues before filing.

This is related to, but distinct from:

- #46366 — **Automatic cost-aware model routing in Codex**, which focuses on automatically choosing the least-expensive capable model/reasoning option.
- #45362 — **Cost-aware adaptive orchestration**, which focuses on dynamic inference/orchestration inside Codex.
- #45133 — **Estimate credits needed to finish an interrupted task**, which focuses on prospective remaining-task cost after interruption.

This request is broader at the **Chat ↔ Work/Codex decision boundary**. It asks for user-authorised access to actual plan capacity so the assistant can recommend *whether to enter Work/Codex at all*, and at what reasoning level, while preserving user authority.

### Additional information

A useful implementation could have graduated permission levels, for example:

1. **No access** — current behavior.
2. **Read-only advisory** — AI may inspect usage and recommend execution/reasoning choices.
3. **User-approved action** — AI may prepare a Work/Codex handoff but asks before starting it.
4. **Delegated within limits** — optional user-defined authority to choose/start execution within explicit constraints.

The read-only advisory level alone would solve most of the current problem.

It would also be useful for the assistant to briefly explain the recommendation, for example:

> This task is suitable for Work, but you have 18% of your current allowance remaining and the reset is tomorrow. I recommend keeping this part in Chat and reserving Work for the implementation step.

That would make usage management part of the agent's decision support rather than a separate manual bookkeeping exercise for the user.

items.body:
## Summary

During a requested re-review of a GitHub PR, Codex ran `gh pr view` inside a workspace-write sandbox with restricted network access. The command failed to connect to `api.github.com`. The agent treated that as a GitHub connectivity problem, reviewed its stale local branch, and reported findings that the submitter had already fixed in a newer PR commit. It then told the user it could not verify the remote head.

A narrowly scoped retry outside the sandbox succeeded immediately with the same `gh` installation and authentication. This is an agent escalation/diagnosis failure, not evidence that GitHub or the user's network was down.

Related: #47658 (closed after its reporter enabled sandbox networking); #31017 covers a different `gh` credential symptom.

## Environment

- Codex CLI 0.158.0, ChatGPT desktop local command execution on macOS 26.5.2
- GitHub CLI 2.96.0
- `workspace-write` sandbox, restricted network, `approvals_reviewer = "auto_review"`
- `gh` authenticated as the expected user through `GITHUB_TOKEN`
- Public PR: https://github.com/7Factor/crap4dotnet/pull/4

## Reproduction and evidence

1. Ask Codex to re-review that PR after the submitter pushes a new commit.
2. Sandboxed `gh pr view 4 --json ...` exits 1: `error connecting to api.github.com`.
3. Sandboxed `git ls-remote origin 'refs/pull/4/head'` exits 128: `ssh: Could not resolve hostname github.com`.
4. Codex continues against local commit `52656cd`, reports two defects, and says GitHub is unavailable. The actual PR head is `6952d40`, which fixes both defects.
5. The same session retries `gh pr view 4 --json number,title,headRefOid,...` with `sandbox_permissions: "require_escalated"`, a read-only `gh pr view` prefix rule, and a narrow justification. It exits 0 and reports `headRefOid: 6952d40...`. `git fetch origin pull/4/head:refs/remotes/origin/pr/4` likewise succeeds with scoped escalation.

No authentication or host-network configuration changed between steps 2 and 5.

## Expected behavior

For a task that requires current remote SCM state, the agent should recognize a restricted-sandbox network/DNS failure, distinguish it from host connectivity or authentication, and retry an authorized read-only SCM command through scoped escalation before reviewing or claiming the PR cannot be verified. If escalation is unavailable or denied, it should stop short of a current-head review and identify the precise boundary.

The product could also make ordinary read-only SCM inspection easier to authorize through a narrow default capability or clearer configuration guidance, while keeping write operations and broad network access separate.

## Actual behavior and impact

The agent reported stale, already-fixed defects as current review findings. The user had to diagnose Codex's execution context and prompt it to use the CLI correctly. This defeats the point of PR re-review and makes sandboxing feel like a misleading failure mode rather than a useful boundary.

### Version and environment

Incident: 2026-09-28, Linux. The recovered rollout session metadata records CLI 0.157.1, originator `codex-tui`, source `vscode`, model `gpt-6-astra`. The user's separate client-debug investigation identifies a `codex-tui 0.157.0` resume at 14:36:56 UTC; these are distinct observations, not a claim that one version string applies to every client. Subscription and terminal version were not checked. This is a historical incident report, not a deterministic reproduction on the latest release.

### Issue

A resumed working session that the user expected to retain full access received a managed restricted permission profile on successive turns. Project files were writable but `.git` was read-only and networking was restricted. This blocked normal Git/gh work. After a later TUI resume, the same thread received full access and work resumed.

Please investigate which client/resume configuration layer supplied the changed profile and why the transition was not clear to the user. I am not asserting that the model edited its configuration or that a provider rejected authentication.

### Independently recovered rollout evidence (UTC)

Thread: `01a0e63e-046b-7e63-a87d-e4f3b6fe8dd9`.

- 13:24:47.394: `approval_policy=never`; resolved `sandbox_policy.type=workspace-write`, `network_access=false`; `permission_profile.type=managed`; filesystem restricted, project root writable, `.git` explicitly read-only; `active_permission_profile.id=:workspace`; network restricted.
- 13:56:52.320: Git/gh returned the errors below.
- 13:56, 14:09, 14:32, 14:35 and 14:36 turn contexts retained the restricted profile.
- 14:11:30.940: Git metadata write still failed with `Read-only file system`.
- 14:11:54.384: the attempted connector write failed with the approval-policy error below.
- 14:37:13.277 and 14:52:50.037: `approval_policy=never`, resolved `sandbox_policy.type=danger-full-access`, `permission_profile.type=disabled`.

```text
error: cannot open '.git/FETCH_HEAD': Read-only file system
error connecting to api.github.com
check your internet connection or https://githubstatus.com
MCP tool call requires approval, but approval policy is never
```

A second local Git error named `.git/index.lock` with `Read-only file system`; the private absolute path is omitted.

### Additional investigator findings (user-supplied)

The user's client-debug investigation reports that afternoon `thread_settings` had `approval_policy: Never`, `sandbox_policy: None`, and a Managed restricted permission profile. It records `thread/resume` at 14:36:56 followed by `permission_profile: None` and successful fetch/push on the next turn. The debug representation of optional settings (`None`) is different from the effective policies serialized in rollout turn contexts above.

The same investigation found no token change, no HTTP 401 and no model edit of the configuration. A fresh read confirmed no sandbox key in `~/.codex/config.toml` and no `/etc/codex/managed_config.toml`. Current configuration alone does not establish historical configuration provenance. The original client-debug events were not independently recovered in this pass.

### User impact and model behavior

Normal commit/push work was interrupted. The assistant compounded this by framing the problem as GitHub rights/write rejection and switching to a GitHub MCP connector before diagnosing the local restriction. The connector was itself unable to write under approval policy Never. Filesystem/socket errors do not establish a provider authorization failure. The model should identify the exact failing layer before switching workflows.

### Expected behavior

Preserve the intended permission profile across resume, or explain and identify the client/config source of a changed profile. Surface effective filesystem/network restrictions clearly enough that the assistant and user can distinguish them from remote authentication failures. Please identify whether this is expected client override behavior or a resume regression.

### Reproduction limits and diagnostics

No deterministic clean reproduction is available. Observed sequence: an existing full-access session was continued after an approximately eight-hour gap; successive turns used a managed restricted profile; a later TUI resume restored full access. No deliberate permission change is reported by the user. Raw logs and a current `codex doctor` dump are omitted because the incident is historical and the full transcript contains unrelated private project material. The bounded evidence above was extracted without uploading that material.

Related, not asserted duplicate causes: #23958 (permission drift on resume), #24570 (permission provenance diagnostics). #40303 involves a renamed workspace, which is not the symptom reported here.

26.924.2738.0 (Microsoft Store package; desktop bundle 26.924.22138)

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

Browser control has failed repeatedly for months across Codex chats. On this Windows desktop app, even a JavaScript call with no browser operation times out and resets the kernel.

`mcp__node_repl__js` with `nodeRepl.write(2)` and a 10-second deadline returns `js execution timed out; kernel reset, rerun your request`. The browser tool's first call, `await cua.getState()`, returns the same error. These failures persist after fully quitting and reopening Codex. The Edge browser extension is installed and enabled, and its native host registration exists. Restarting the computer-use helper and the extension host did not fix the failure.

This blocks ordinary signed-in browser work. No site navigation, login, or page action is needed to reproduce the minimal JavaScript timeout.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Windows, open a Codex Desktop chat with the JavaScript and browser-control tools available.
2. Call `mcp__node_repl__js` with `{ "code": "nodeRepl.write(2)", "timeout_ms": 10000 }`. Observe `js execution timed out; kernel reset, rerun your request`.
3. In a fresh browser-control session, call `mcp__cua_repl.js` with `{ "code": "await cua.getState();", "timeout_ms": 10000 }`. Observe the same timeout and reset.
4. Fully quit and reopen Codex Desktop, then repeat. The failure remains.

Control: the installed Node executable completes the calculation. A separately launched `node_repl.exe` MCP process returns `2` promptly, both with and without `CODEX_CLI_PATH` set.

### What is the expected behavior?

`nodeRepl.write(2)` should return `2` promptly. The browser inventory should return available browser state or a specific actionable error. A failed call should not hang until the JavaScript kernel resets.

### Additional information

Codex desktop bundle: 26.924.22138; Microsoft Store package: OpenAI.Codex 26.924.2738.0. The extension host relaunched after a targeted restart, but the app-managed calls still timed out. A separately launched `cua-repl` process executed JavaScript but could not inspect browsers because it lacked Codex turn metadata; that test does not establish working browser access. The default command sandbox separately reports that it cannot enforce split writable roots; whether this contributes to the Node REPL failure is unknown.

items.title: Preserve pending environments when spawning subagents
items.body:
Preserve pending environments when spawning subagents

## Why

Spawning a subagent before an environment was ready dropped the starting environment from the child's selections. The child needs to retain that environment and receive its configuration or failure when preparation finishes.

## What changed

- Pass the spawning step's environment snapshot to children, preserving ready and starting environments and configuration ownership.
- Propagate the original owner's first configuration result through descendants, applying each session's validation and leaving independently configured children unchanged.
- Preserve pending configuration waits across executor retries. Later owner updates do not overwrite the child's inherited configuration.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for fresh and forked subagents, readiness through turn-settings updates, failure propagation to children and grandchildren, child configuration precedence, and executor retries. Add a request snapshot showing a child using `wait_for_environment` before execution tools become available.

items.title: Reclaim unused SQLite log database pages in the background
items.body:
Reclaim unused SQLite log database pages in the background

## Why

Deleting logs leaves free SQLite pages available for reuse without shrinking the database file. Reclaim excess free space while preserving a reserve for future writes.

## What changed

- Start a background incremental-vacuum worker with `StateRuntime`, enabling reclamation only for the logs database. Use a per-home file lock to select one worker and wait for it to finish during shutdown.
- Reclaim pages when at least 64 MiB and 25% of the database are free, preserving a reserve of at least 16 MiB or 10% of the database.
- Use short transactions with page and cooperative time budgets, defer work on contention, and reduce batch sizes with exponential backoff when interrupted passes make no progress.
- Record reclamation counts, durations, and reclaimed pages in telemetry.

## Testing

Add a regression test that interrupts a vacuum commit, verifies foreground writes can resume without data loss, then confirms a resumed pass shrinks the database and passes `PRAGMA integrity_check`.

## Summary

After a Codex Desktop task finished on Windows, the assistant twice told the user that it had stopped its local test servers. The Desktop UI still showed **“12 background terminals running”**. This was not only a stale UI count: an OS process inspection found live processes from that task.

## Environment

- Codex Desktop: 26.924.2738.0
- Windows 11 Pro, build 26200
- Observed on 2026-09-28, America/Sao_Paulo
- Task: build and test a Blazor WebAssembly mobile prototype
- Model shown in the Desktop UI: gpt-6-sol, xhigh

## Observed sequence

1. The agent started several long-running development/test commands through terminal tools: `dotnet run` / Blazor dev servers, Python static servers, and Playwright Node scripts.
2. At the end of the task, the agent sent Ctrl+C to the session IDs it knew and reported that the servers had been closed.
3. The user asked whether work was still running. The agent again answered that it had finished and closed the servers.
4. The user pointed to the Desktop indicator: **“12 background terminals running”**.
5. A read-only Windows process inspection showed live task-related `dotnet.exe`, `blazor-devserver.dll`, `python.exe`, `node.exe`, and PowerShell wrappers. Ports 5240–5248 were among the local test ports.
6. Targeted cleanup of only the task-related process trees found 78 candidate processes/descendants; 51 were still stoppable at cleanup time. A follow-up check found **zero matching processes and zero listeners on ports 5240–5248**. The user confirmed that `/stop` resolved the remaining background-terminal indicator.

No unrelated process was intentionally stopped. Local paths, account details, and screenshots are omitted from this public report.

## Expected behavior

- The agent should verify process-tree and port state before claiming that its background servers are stopped.
- Stopping a terminal session should terminate or clearly surface its surviving child processes.
- A completed task should not leave test commands running silently, and the Desktop terminal indicator should reflect the actual state.

## Reproduction status

This is one observed incident, not a verified minimal reproducer. The likely workflow is to launch several nested long-running commands during a coding task, send Ctrl+C to the known terminal sessions, and finish the turn without checking the child processes.

Related but distinct: #12321 concerns a stale Desktop count after processes are already dead. Here the count exposed **real live processes**. #29079 discusses retained Windows helper processes, while this report includes development and test processes spawned by the agent.

### What variant of Codex are you using?

App

### What feature would you like to see?

This may be related to #25983 and #30900, but the specific missing capability here is a safe first-class path for persisting Browser screenshots into the workspace.

## Feature request: Safe way to save Browser screenshots to workspace

### Problem

Codex Browser can capture screenshots and return them to the current session, but there does not appear to be a supported way to persist those screenshots as image files inside the workspace/project.

This becomes a practical limitation for workflows such as:

- writing operation manuals
- generating Word/PDF documentation
- creating UI test evidence
- annotating screenshots with arrows, boxes, numbers, or notes
- keeping before/after screenshots together with project files

In my case, Codex successfully captured the required screenshots, but could not save them into the project for later use in Word/PDF generation.

The agent then tried to place the screenshot into a temporary page and export it as a local file. This was correctly blocked by the Browser URL policy, which also prohibited using indirect browser/CDP workarounds.

So the current behavior creates an awkward gap:

**Browser can obtain the image, but there is no supported path from that image to a project file.**

### Suggested solution

Instead of relaxing the general Browser URL policy or allowing arbitrary Blob/data/file exports, Codex could provide a narrow, dedicated API such as:

`save_browser_screenshot(image_handle, workspace_path)`

or:

`save_image_artifact(image_handle, workspace_path)`

The capability could be restricted to verified image formats such as PNG and JPEG.

For additional safety, the implementation could:

- actually decode the image instead of trusting MIME type or file extension
- optionally re-encode the decoded bitmap before saving
- strip unnecessary metadata
- limit maximum image dimensions and file size
- only allow writing inside the current workspace or explicitly approved directories
- require user confirmation when needed

### Why this seems like a reasonable security tradeoff

The goal is not to provide a generic:

**Browser/session data → arbitrary local file**

bridge.

It would instead provide a much narrower path:

**Browser screenshot → validated bitmap → workspace image file**

That is significantly less powerful than allowing arbitrary Blob downloads, `data:` URLs, `file://` navigation, raw CDP export, or other general-purpose browser-to-filesystem mechanisms.

In fact, providing an official narrow path may improve security, because users and agents would no longer be encouraged to invent temporary HTML/Blob/CDP workarounds just to save a screenshot.

### Expected result

Browser screenshots could be safely persisted into the project and then processed by normal local tools such as Pillow, ImageMagick, Word/PDF generators, or documentation pipelines.

This would make Browser Use much more practical for documentation and UI-review workflows without weakening the broader Browser URL security model.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.908.70816

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Ubuntu 26.04

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex in the ChatGPT desktop application on Linux becomes stuck on essentially any prompt and does not complete the request.

The underlying Codex installation, authentication, network connectivity, WebSocket connection, configuration, sandbox, and state databases appear healthy.

Most importantly, the **same Codex binary bundled with the ChatGPT desktop application works correctly when executed directly with `--no-daemon`**.

The problem therefore appears specific to the **ChatGPT Desktop → Codex app-server / MCP integration path**, rather than a general Codex connectivity or authentication failure.



### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Just chat with Codex.

### What is the expected behavior?



Desktop application installation:

`/usr/lib/chatgpt/ChatGPT`

Desktop application build observed in Codex configuration/environment:

``

Bundled Codex executable:

`/usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex`

Codex version:

`codex-cli 0.158.0-alpha.2.1`

Git:

`/usr/bin/git`

Git version:

`2.53.0`

Codex authentication mode:

ChatGPT authentication

## Primary Symptom

Normal ChatGPT conversations in the desktop application work.

Codex mode in the same desktop application starts, but prompts generally remain stuck and do not complete.

Even a trivial prompt such as:

`Reply with exactly: CODEX WORKS`

can hang.

## Important Control Test

The Codex binary bundled with the desktop application was executed directly:

`/usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex --no-daemon`

This works correctly.

Codex can operate on a test workspace and respond normally when launched this way.

This suggests that the underlying Codex runtime and account access are functional.

## Codex Doctor Results

Running:

`/usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex doctor`

reports:

- Configuration loaded successfully
- Authentication configured successfully
- ChatGPT tokens present
- State databases healthy
- Thread inventory consistent
- Sandbox initialized
- Network configuration valid
- WebSocket connected successfully
- HTTP 101 Switching Protocols received
- OpenAI provider endpoints reachable
- 0 failed diagnostic tests

Summary:

`18 ok · 1 idle · 2 notes · 2 warn · 0 fail degraded`

The two warnings were:

1. `rg` / ripgrep could not initially be verified.
2. Terminal height below the recommended 24 rows.

Neither appears sufficient to explain the desktop Codex hang.

## Network / Authentication Evidence

Codex Doctor successfully establishes a WebSocket connection to the ChatGPT backend:

`websocket connected (HTTP 101 Switching Protocols)`

The active OpenAI provider endpoints are also reachable over HTTP.

Authentication is stored in ChatGPT mode and ChatGPT tokens are present.

This makes a basic network or authentication failure unlikely.

## Desktop App-Server Evidence

While the desktop application is running, it launches:

`/usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex -c features.code_mode_host=true app-server --analytics-default-enabled -c plugins.codex-app-tools@openai-bundled.mcp_servers.codex_app.enabled=true`

Therefore, the desktop application is successfully starting the Codex app-server process.

The desktop logs also show successful app-server calls including:

- `model/list`
- `permissionProfile/list`
- `config/read`
- `account/read`
- `getAuthStatus`
- `experimentalFeature/list`
- `app/installed`
- `app/read`
- `skills/list`

These requests return:

`errorCode=null`

So basic communication between the Electron desktop application and the Codex app-server is functioning.

## Potentially Significant Error #1: MCP Method Not Found

The desktop application logs report:

`Failed to list resource templates for MCP server 'codex_app': Mcp error: -32601: Method not found`

Target:

`codex_mcp::connection_manager::resources`

This may indicate a protocol/API compatibility mismatch between the desktop application's Codex integration and the bundled `codex_app` MCP server.

Please investigate whether the desktop build and bundled Codex/MCP components expect different MCP capabilities or protocol versions.

## Potentially Significant Error #2: Invalid Experimental Feature

The desktop logs also report:

`ignoring invalid experimental feature enablement keys: apps_mcp_path_override`

Target:

`codex_app_server::request_processors::config_processor`

This suggests that one component of the desktop application is supplying an experimental feature key that the bundled Codex app-server does not recognize.

Combined with the MCP `-32601 Method not found` response, this raises the possibility of incompatible desktop/Codex component versions.

## Potentially Significant Error #3: Git Reported Unavailable

The desktop application repeatedly reports:

`[managed-worktree-archive-queue] Worktree archive will be retried errorMessage="Git is unavailable"`

However, Git is installed and fully accessible:

`which git`
→ `/usr/bin/git`

`git --version`
→ `git version 2.53.0`

`/usr/bin/git --version`
→ `git version 2.53.0`

The shell PATH includes:

`/usr/bin`

Codex Doctor also detects Git successfully.

The ChatGPT desktop application was additionally launched with a minimal PATH:

`env PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin /usr/lib/chatgpt/ChatGPT`

The `Git is unavailable` message persisted.

Therefore, this does not appear to be a normal PATH or missing-Git problem.

It may be an issue with the desktop application's managed-worktree worker or its Git discovery/execution mechanism.

It is not yet clear whether this Git error causes the prompt hang or is an unrelated archive/cleanup failure.

## Additional Process Observation

During one stuck desktop Codex session, the process list contained a defunct Codex child:

`[codex] <defunct>`

At the same time, the desktop Codex `app-server` process remained running.

This may be relevant to child-process lifecycle management in the desktop integration.

## Other Log Messages

The Electron/Chromium logs contain:

`Registration response error message: DEPRECATED_ENDPOINT`

from:

`google_apis/gcm/engine/registration_request.cc`

There are also WebRTC messages such as:

`DcSctpTransport->ResetStream: Transport is not started.`

These may be unrelated Chromium/Electron warnings, but they are included here for completeness.

## Configuration

The Codex configuration parses successfully.

Current model configuration includes:

`model = "gpt-6-astra"`

`model_reasoning_effort = "low"`

`service_tier = "priority"`

There is no deprecated:

`approval_policy = "untrusted"`

setting.

Codex Doctor reports the effective approval policy as:

`OnRequest`

and filesystem/network sandboxing as restricted.

## Reproduction Procedure

1. Start the ChatGPT Linux desktop application.

2. Open Codex mode.

3. Select or create a small local workspace.

4. Submit a trivial prompt, for example:

   `Reply with exactly: CODEX WORKS`

5. Codex becomes stuck and does not complete normally.

6. Quit the desktop application.

7. From the same machine and account, run:

   `/usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex --no-daemon`

8. Submit a comparable trivial request.

9. The CLI Codex session works.

## Expected Behaviour

Codex running through the ChatGPT desktop application should complete the request in the same way that the bundled Codex executable does when launched using `--no-daemon`.

## Actual Behaviour

Codex requests through the desktop application hang, while direct execution of the bundled Codex runtime works.

## Requested Engineering Investigation

Could the Codex/Desktop engineering team please check:

1. Whether ChatGPT Desktop build `26.908.70816` is expected to bundle `codex-cli 0.158.0-alpha.2.1`.

2. Whether the desktop build and bundled Codex app-server/MCP implementation are protocol-compatible.

3. Why `codex_app` returns:

   `Mcp error: -32601: Method not found`

   when resource templates are requested.

4. Why the desktop application enables:

   `apps_mcp_path_override`

   while the bundled app-server reports that feature key as invalid.

5. Why the desktop managed-worktree worker reports:

   `Git is unavailable`

   despite `/usr/bin/git` being available and executable.

6. Whether the observed `[codex] <defunct>` child process indicates a failed subprocess that the app-server/UI continues waiting for.

7. Whether the desktop application can temporarily fall back to the equivalent of `--no-daemon`, given that this execution path works correctly on the same machine.

## Suggested Fix / Workaround

A useful engineering workaround would be to allow the desktop client to use the functioning non-daemon Codex execution path if app-server initialization or MCP capability negotiation fails.

If the issue is caused by mismatched bundled components, please provide or push a desktop build containing mutually compatible versions of:

- ChatGPT Desktop
- Codex app-server
- `codex_app` MCP server/plugin
- bundled OpenAI plugins

In particular, please verify MCP capability negotiation before requesting `resources/templates/list` or equivalent functionality and ensure that experimental feature flags sent by the desktop client are supported by the bundled app-server.

## Current Workaround

Codex can currently be used successfully from the terminal with:

`/usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex --no-daemon`

The problem appears confined to Codex execution through the ChatGPT desktop application's integration layer.

### Additional information

_No response_

I have trouble shot this with Chatgpt and have a solution.. for now. The UI hangs EVERY time I fully close out of codes desktop and then reopen the application. Chatgpt and I have determined the backend is healthy, the session authenticates with OpenAI, but the UI hangs and that is the issue.

**Feedback ID:** no-active-thread-01a0e92f-7216-7083-9885-fb1813ff896d

**Chatgpt diag:**
Windows 11, build 26100
Codex Desktop 26.924.2738.0
Codex CLI 0.158.0-alpha.2.1
Desktop process launches normally
app-server launches and initializes successfully
ChatGPT authentication succeeds
WebSocket connectivity succeeds
CDN connectivity succeeds
configuration parses successfully
Codex databases pass integrity checks
desktop renderer remains on the loading spinner
startup eventually records app_start outcome=failure reason=timeout
**killing only the codex.exe app-server child while leaving the Electron desktop process running causes it to respawn
UI becomes functional roughly 15 seconds later**
no deletion/reset/reinstallation is required

**Chatgpt Powershell solution:**
$servers = Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='codex.exe'" |
    Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -match 'app-server' }

$servers | Select-Object ProcessId, ParentProcessId, CommandLine

if ($servers) {
    $servers | ForEach-Object {
        Write-Host "Restarting Codex app-server PID $($_.ProcessId)"
        Stop-Process -Id $_.ProcessId -Force
    }
} else {
    Write-Host "NO_CODEX_APP_SERVER_FOUND"
}

items.title: Codex 0.158.0 hangs in tmux when startup probe selects incompatible tmux client

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: TUI
labels.description: Issues related to the terminal user interface: text input, menus and dialogs, and terminal display

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
## Summary

Codex CLI `0.158.0` can hang indefinitely before rendering the TUI when running inside tmux if the tmux client selected by Codex's startup probe is incompatible with the active tmux server.

This is a regression from `0.153.4`, which starts successfully in the same environment.

## Environment

- OS: Linux x86_64
- Codex CLI: `0.158.0`
- Active tmux server: `3.1b`, custom installation/socket
- System tmux client: `/usr/bin/tmux` `2.7`
- Interactive shell resolves `tmux` to the matching `3.1b` wrapper before `/usr/bin`

## Reproduction

1. Start or attach to a tmux `3.1b` server using a custom socket.
2. Have tmux `2.7` installed at `/usr/bin/tmux`.
3. Configure the interactive shell's `PATH` so `tmux` resolves to the matching `3.1b` wrapper before `/usr/bin`.
4. Run Codex CLI `0.158.0` inside a tmux pane.

## Actual behavior

Codex hangs before rendering the TUI.

The blocked startup path creates:

```
/usr/bin/tmux display-message -p -t %14 #{extended-keys-format}.#{mouse}
```

The tmux process remains blocked in `poll`, while Codex waits for it to complete.

The Codex parent has the expected user `PATH`, including the custom tmux wrapper. However, the probe child receives a minimal path similar to:

```
/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/usr/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/sbin
```

As a result, the probe launches `/usr/bin/tmux` rather than the matching `3.1b` client.

## Expected behavior

A tmux capability probe should not be able to block Codex startup indefinitely.

Codex should either:

- resolve `tmux` consistently with the parent environment,
- support explicitly configuring the tmux executable, and/or
- bound the probe with a timeout and continue startup with conservative defaults if it fails.

## Evidence / isolation

The issue can be isolated to the tmux startup probe:

- The capability query returns immediately with the matching tmux `3.1b` client.
- The same query using `/usr/bin/tmux` `2.7` blocks.
- Mapping the matching `3.1b` client over `/usr/bin/tmux` only for the Codex process allows `0.158.0` to start normally.
- Unsetting `TMUX` and `TMUX_PANE` before starting Codex also avoids the hang.
- Codex CLI `0.153.4` starts successfully in the same environment.

## Configuration workarounds tried

The following did not prevent the probe from launching `/usr/bin/tmux`:

```
CODEX_TUI_DISABLE_KEYBOARD_ENHANCEMENT=1
shell_environment_policy.inherit="all"
shell_environment_policy.set.PATH="<custom tmux path>:/usr/bin:/bin"
```

`CODEX_TUI_DISABLE_KEYBOARD_ENHANCEMENT=1` was confirmed present in both the Codex process and the blocked tmux child.

Disabling keyboard enhancement does not eliminate this probe because it also queries tmux mouse state.

## Likely failure path

```
Codex 0.158.0
    |
    +-- detects TMUX / TMUX_PANE
    |
    +-- starts tmux capability probe
            |
            +-- resolves /usr/bin/tmux
            |
            +-- display-message
                    "#{extended-keys-format}.#{mouse}"
            |
            +-- incompatible client/server interaction blocks
                    |
                    +-- Codex waits indefinitely
```

The key robustness issue is not only which tmux executable is selected: an external capability probe can block TUI initialization without a timeout.

## Suggested fix

### 1. Bound the tmux probe

Apply a short timeout to the `tmux display-message` invocation.

If the command fails, cannot connect, or times out, continue startup with conservative capability defaults rather than blocking TUI initialization.

### 2. Fix tmux executable resolution

Resolve `tmux` from the intended parent environment rather than an environment that causes `/usr/bin/tmux` to be selected unexpectedly.

Alternatively, provide a supported configuration option such as:

```
tui.tmux_path = "/path/to/tmux"
```

### 3. Treat capability detection as best-effort

Failure to determine `extended-keys-format` or `mouse` should degrade functionality rather than prevent Codex from starting.

## Regression

| Version | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `0.153.4` | Starts normally |
| `0.158.0` | Hangs before TUI |

items.title: Desktop: opt-in detailed UI performance traces with invalidation causes and capture-quality reporting

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
> **Status update — September 30, 2026:** After updating to 26.928.20755 (build 12246), the reporting user no longer observes the first-character/last-character composer stalls. This is subjective follow-up, not a timed validation. The trace and recorder inspection below are historical evidence from 26.924.22138; the new build's detailed-capture capabilities have not been revalidated. This request remains about diagnostic capability rather than claiming that the original symptom is still present. See the [updated report](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48659#issuecomment-5865340696).

### What variant of Codex are you using?

Desktop app / local Codex surface in ChatGPT Desktop 26.924.22138 (build 11645), macOS 27.0, Apple Silicon.

### What feature would you like to see?

**An opt-in detailed UI performance capture that records style-invalidation causes and selector costs, correlates them with interactions, and reports what diagnostic data was actually collected.**

The ordinary recorder should remain available for measuring responsiveness. Detailed capture should be a separate, bounded diagnostic mode because it adds overhead and may contain more sensitive data.

#### Why this matters

In [the macOS evidence on #48659](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48659#issuecomment-5865340696), one keyboard event in the built-in recording took **727.792 ms from input generation to compositor presentation**, alongside repeated broad style recalculation. This is a profiled sample, not an unprofiled latency baseline or a population statistic. We can identify geometry/style reads that force pending recalculation, but cannot identify the original invalidating DOM change or expensive selector from that recording. Repeating the same capture configuration does not address this observability gap.

Read-only inspection of that installed build found the explicitly included categories:

```text
*
disabled-by-default-v8.cpu_profiler
disabled-by-default-v8.cpu_profiler.hires
```

The retained trace metadata confirms these categories were requested, with an additional metadata category. Chromium [handles disabled-by-default categories separately from `*`](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/154.0.8037.57/base/trace_event/trace_config_category_filter.cc). The recording contains no style-invalidation-tracking or `SelectorStats` records. Requested configuration and observed events are distinct evidence; event absence alone does not establish why data is missing.

The current recorder already has a finite buffer, a capacity-triggered stop and a Keep local option. The proposal below extends those safeguards for detailed capture.

#### Proposed acceptance criteria

1. **Explicit mode and limits.** Offer ordinary and detailed captures. Preserve the existing buffer/capacity stop, add a duration limit for detailed mode, and report known truncation/loss plus profiler-startup intervals. State when loss status is unavailable.
2. **Verified instrumentation.** Enable supported style-invalidation and selector-cost instrumentation. Record requested and observable active capabilities, unsupported options and unknown status where activation cannot be verified. Verify actual events on a known invalidation fixture rather than assuming category strings suffice. DevTools exposes [these categories](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/devtools-frontend/blob/main/front_end/models/trace/types/TraceEvents.ts) and [an explicit selector-stats capture option](https://github.com/ChromeDevTools/devtools-frontend/blob/main/front_end/panels/timeline/TimelineController.ts).
3. **Content-free interaction markers.** Record operation kind and monotonic timestamp for composer empty/nonempty transitions, chat switching and attachment-flow start. Do not put prompt text, key values, conversation identifiers, filenames or file contents in these markers. Distinguish action initiation from rendering completion.
4. **Actionable capture summary.** Use a common trace timebase to align markers with EventTiming/EventLatency where available; distinguish confirmed presentation endpoints from fallback timing without summing overlapping records. List diagnostic event counts and distinguish unsupported, not enabled, no applicable event and indeterminate outcomes. Zero events must not silently mean a healthy app or a disabled category.
5. **Local-first handling.** Preserve the existing Keep local path and make upload a separate choice. Provide a shareable aggregate summary separately from the raw trace. Content-free markers do not make the entire trace anonymous: stacks, URLs, selectors and attributes still require privacy review.
6. **Test the recorder itself.** Use a deterministic local fixture to verify invalidation/selector event capture. Compare unprofiled, ordinary and detailed modes with matched workloads. Use unprofiled interaction measurements as the performance baseline and traces to explain observed work. Ordinary capture also adds overhead; startup intervals and sample sizes must be reported.

### Additional information

This is a diagnostic feature request, not another report of the same input-lag defect, and not a claim that detailed tracing guarantees a root cause. #48659 tracks the observed responsiveness problem. This request makes future user recordings useful for distinguishing the operation that dirties styles from the later read that pays the cost.

Only sanitized findings are included here; no raw trace or private application data is attached.

items.title: Flaky test: image_preparation::tests::detail_policies_apply_the_expected_budgets times out under load

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

The unit test `image_preparation::tests::detail_policies_apply_the_expected_budgets` is flaky. In 20 full runs of
the `codex-core` test suite with retries disabled, it **timed out 2 times** (iterations 1 and 2) and passed 18 times,
with no code change.

Passing runs took **54.4–58.7 s**. nextest kills a test after 60 s
(`codex-rs/.config/nextest.toml`: `slow-timeout = { period = "30s", terminate-after = 2 }`).
Exact output of a failing run:

```
     TIMEOUT [  60.023s] (1887/4454) codex-core image_preparation::tests::detail_policies_apply_the_expected_budgets
```

The two timeouts happened in the slowest iterations of the run (iteration 1 took 985 s vs ~765 s for the others).

Tested at commit [`96aca987f7`](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/96aca987f72e29a639ecabe5b76ccd6e5693fc88).
**Still present on `main`** (checked 2026-09-28): the test is at `image_preparation_tests.rs:148` there, with the same
five image cases (only one extra argument was added to a call). There is no per-test timeout override or dev-profile
optimization for the image crates in `main`'s `.config/nextest.toml` or `Cargo.toml`. Line numbers below are for the
tested commit and link to it.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?


```bash
cd codex-rs
# alone: passes, but takes ~38 s
cargo nextest run -p codex-core --retries 0 --stress-count 2 \
  -E 'test(=image_preparation::tests::detail_policies_apply_the_expected_budgets)'
# 37.9 s, 37.9 s

# under load (4 CPUs here; one busy loop per CPU)
for i in 1 2 3 4; do ( timeout 600 sh -c 'while :; do :; done' ) & done
cargo nextest run -p codex-core --retries 0 --no-fail-fast --stress-count 3 \
  -E 'test(=image_preparation::tests::detail_policies_apply_the_expected_budgets)'
kill $(jobs -p)
# result: TIMEOUT 3/3
```


### What is the expected behavior?

The test finishes well within the 60 s per-test limit, so machine load doesn't decide the result.


### Additional information

**Root cause (measured):**

- The code and the test logic are correct; the test is just expensive in an unoptimized (debug) build.
- The test ([`image_preparation_tests.rs:147`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/96aca987f72e29a639ecabe5b76ccd6e5693fc88/codex-rs/core/src/image_preparation_tests.rs#L147))
  creates, encodes, resizes and decodes PNGs of up to ~10 megapixels. Per-case timing (temporary timers, test run
  alone, 37.8 s total):

  | Case | Test creates PNG | `prepare_response_items` (resize + encode) | Test decodes |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | High 2048² → 1600² | 2.9 s | 4.5 s | 0.2 s |
  | Original 6401×100 → 6000×94 | 0.4 s | 0.8 s | 0.0 s |
  | Original 3201² → 3200² | 7.0 s | 15.2 s | 0.7 s |
  | Auto 2048² → 1600² | 2.8 s | 0.0 s (image cache hit) | 0.2 s |
  | None 2048² → 1600² | 2.8 s | 0.0 s (image cache hit) | 0.2 s |

  The 3201² case is 61% of the time, and the test's own input creation
  ([`png_data_url`, lines 49–57](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/96aca987f72e29a639ecabe5b76ccd6e5693fc88/codex-rs/core/src/image_preparation_tests.rs#L49-L57)) is 42%.
- `perf` shows the time in PNG encoding (`png::filter::filter_internal`, `filter_paeth_fpnge`, `sum_buffer`) and
  resizing (`image::imageops::sample::vertical_sample`), with debug-only overhead
  (`slice::from_raw_parts::precondition_check`, uninlined `Ord::max`/`Ord::min`). The Codex code involved:
  `resize_exact(…, FilterType::Triangle)`
  ([`utils/image/src/lib.rs:174`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/96aca987f72e29a639ecabe5b76ccd6e5693fc88/codex-rs/utils/image/src/lib.rs#L174))
  and `encode_image`
  ([lines 363–392](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/96aca987f72e29a639ecabe5b76ccd6e5693fc88/codex-rs/utils/image/src/lib.rs#L363-L392)).

**Suggested fix:** build the image crates optimized in the dev/test profile (`codex-rs/Cargo.toml`):

```toml
[profile.dev.package.png]
opt-level = 3
[profile.dev.package.image]
opt-level = 3
[profile.dev.package.fdeflate]
opt-level = 3
[profile.dev.package.flate2]
opt-level = 3
[profile.dev.package.miniz_oxide]
opt-level = 3
[profile.dev.package.crc32fast]
opt-level = 3
```

Checked locally by applying the same settings with `cargo nextest run --config profile.dev.package.<crate>.opt-level=3 …`:

| Build | Alone | Under 4-loop CPU load |
|---|---|---|
| Current | 37.9 s | TIMEOUT 3/3 |
| Image crates at `opt-level = 3` | **5.3 s** | **10.3–10.7 s** (3/3 pass) |

Optional, in addition: reuse the generated 2048² input across the three cases that use it (saves ~5.6 s), and/or
split the cases into separate tests. Splitting alone isn't enough, because the 3201² case is ~23 s by itself.

**Environment:**
- Commit `96aca987f72e29a639ecabe5b76ccd6e5693fc88`
- `Linux 7.0.0-1013-aws x86_64` (Ubuntu 26.04 LTS), 4 CPUs, 15 GiB RAM
- rustc 1.95.0, cargo-nextest 0.9.145
- Run with `just test -p codex-core --retries 0`, 20 full runs of all 4,454 codex-core tests, started without a terminal (`setsid`)

items.title: Flaky test: permission_request_hook_allows_exec_command_without_user_approval races with a sibling test on a shared /tmp file

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: hooks
labels.description: Issues related to event hooks

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

The integration test `suite::hooks::permission_request_hook_allows_exec_command_without_user_approval` is flaky.
In 20 full runs of the `codex-core` test suite with retries disabled, it **failed 3 times** (iterations 6, 7 and 15)
and passed 17 times, with no code change.

Exact output of a failing run (the number in parentheses is the thread id, which differs per run):

```
thread 'suite::hooks::permission_request_hook_allows_exec_command_without_user_approval' (1539822) panicked at core/tests/suite/hooks.rs:3046:5:
approved command should remove marker file
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
```
Tested at commit [`96aca987f7`](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/96aca987f72e29a639ecabe5b76ccd6e5693fc88).
**Still present on `main`** (checked 2026-09-28): the test code is unchanged there, only a few lines lower
(the test starts at `hooks.rs:2993`, the shared path is at lines 2998 and 3291). Line numbers below are for the tested commit and link to it.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The natural failure depends on timing. The mechanism can be reproduced deterministically by rewriting
the shared marker file in the background while the test runs (this simulates the sibling test described below):

```bash
cd codex-rs
M=/tmp/permissionrequest-exec-command-marker
( end=$((SECONDS+100)); while [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do echo seed > $M; sleep 0.05; done ) &
cargo nextest run -p codex-core --retries 0 --no-fail-fast --stress-count 5 \
  -E 'test(=suite::hooks::permission_request_hook_allows_exec_command_without_user_approval)'
# result: 0 passed, 5 failed, all with "approved command should remove marker file"
kill %1; rm -f $M
# same command without the background loop: 5/5 passed
```

To see it happen naturally, run the full suite repeatedly with retries off:
`just test -p codex-core --retries 0` (it failed 3 times in 20 runs here).

### What is the expected behavior?

The test passes regardless of which other tests run at the same time. It should not share
filesystem state with other tests.

### Additional information

**Root cause (from the code and the run logs):**

- The test builds its marker path with a fixed name in the system temp directory
  ([`hooks.rs:3002`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/96aca987f72e29a639ecabe5b76ccd6e5693fc88/codex-rs/core/tests/suite/hooks.rs#L3002)):
  ```rust
  let marker = std::env::temp_dir().join("permissionrequest-exec-command-marker");
  ```
  It writes `"seed"` to it
  ([line 3034](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/96aca987f72e29a639ecabe5b76ccd6e5693fc88/codex-rs/core/tests/suite/hooks.rs#L3034)),
  has Codex run `rm -f <marker>` (approved by the PermissionRequest hook), and then asserts the file is gone
  ([lines 3046–3049](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/96aca987f72e29a639ecabe5b76ccd6e5693fc88/codex-rs/core/tests/suite/hooks.rs#L3046-L3049)).
- The sibling test `suite::hooks::permission_request_hook_sees_raw_exec_command_input`
  ([`hooks.rs:3289`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/96aca987f72e29a639ecabe5b76ccd6e5693fc88/codex-rs/core/tests/suite/hooks.rs#L3289))
  uses **the same path**
  ([line 3294](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/96aca987f72e29a639ecabe5b76ccd6e5693fc88/codex-rs/core/tests/suite/hooks.rs#L3294))
  and writes `"seed"` to it too
  ([line 3334](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/96aca987f72e29a639ecabe5b76ccd6e5693fc88/codex-rs/core/tests/suite/hooks.rs#L3334)).
- nextest runs the two tests in parallel, in separate processes that share `/tmp`. If the sibling's write lands
  between this test's `rm -f` and its `!marker.exists()` check, the check fails. In all 20 runs the two tests
  finished next to each other in the nextest output (they always overlap in time). In all 3 failures the sibling
  finished immediately after with almost the same duration (0.802 s / 0.805 s, 0.811 s / 0.830 s, 0.810 s / 0.814 s).
- Either test can be the victim; in these runs it was always this one.

**Suggested fix:** give each test its own marker in a private temp directory, the same pattern already used by
`pre_tool_use_json_deny_blocks_exec_command_before_execution`
([`hooks.rs:3531–3532`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/96aca987f72e29a639ecabe5b76ccd6e5693fc88/codex-rs/core/tests/suite/hooks.rs#L3531-L3532)).
In both tests:

```diff
-    let marker = std::env::temp_dir().join("permissionrequest-exec-command-marker");
+    let marker_dir = TempDir::new()?;
+    let marker = marker_dir.path().join("permissionrequest-exec-command-marker");
```

(`TempDir` is already imported in `hooks.rs`.) Checked locally: with this change, both tests passed **10/10**
while the background loop above kept rewriting the old `/tmp` path.

**Environment:**
- Commit `96aca987f72e29a639ecabe5b76ccd6e5693fc88`
- `Linux 7.0.0-1013-aws x86_64` (Ubuntu 26.04 LTS), 4 CPUs, 15 GiB RAM
- rustc 1.95.0, cargo-nextest 0.9.145
- Run with `just test -p codex-core --retries 0`, 20 full runs of all 4,454 codex-core tests, started without a terminal (`setsid`)
