items.title: Add opt-in conversation history retrieval to Guardian reviews
items.body:
Add opt-in conversation history retrieval to Guardian reviews

## Why

The transcript supplied to Guardian may omit earlier user instructions, restrictions, or revoked permissions. History retrieval lets the reviewer check relevant authorization before approving actions with side effects.

## What changed

- Add the disabled-by-default `guardian_conversation_history_tools` feature. With Apps enabled, expose `user_message.search_messages` and `user_message.read_messages` through the parent's live Apps connection and conversation identity.
- Recheck the parent's current app and tool policy on each call, rejecting disabled tools and calls requiring approval.
- Add retrieval instructions that distinguish user authorization from assistant context and account for later revocations and incomplete results. Allow overrides through `auto_review.experimental_conversation_history_prompt`.
- Limit history responses to an estimated 4,000 tokens by default, configurable through `auto_review.conversation_history_max_output_tokens`, while preserving stricter parent and reviewer limits.
- Allow explicit extension registries for isolated sessions and prevent those sessions from inheriting the implicit Apps connection.

items.title: Avoid SQLite stalls from connection setup and stderr span logging
items.body:
Avoid SQLite stalls from connection setup and stderr span logging

## Why

Setting `auto_vacuum` on every connection can wait for a writer lock even when the mode is unchanged. Logging every span entry and exit can also block SQLx workers on undrained stderr while they hold a write transaction.

## What changed

- Set incremental vacuum only for empty databases or databases using full auto-vacuum, before enabling WAL. Preserve existing nonempty databases with auto-vacuum disabled.
- Emit span creation and closure events in app-server text and JSON stderr logs, preserving busy/idle timings and explicit events while omitting span entry and exit records.

## Testing

Add regression tests for opening and expanding writable pools while another connection holds a writer lock, and for transaction completion with undrained stderr in both log formats. Verify vacuum modes and retained log diagnostics.

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.158.0-alpha.2.1 (bundled binary)

### What subscription do you have?

Not applicable to this reproduction: isolated CODEX_HOME, local mock provider, no login or model request.

### Which model were you using?

Local mock provider (probe-model); no inference request was needed.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS, Apple Silicon (arm64)

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Not applicable; codex app-server --stdio launched from a Python subprocess.

### Codex doctor report

```json

```

### What issue are you seeing?

Hi! Completed startup operations such as `thread/start` and `session_init` appear to remain unexported while an MCP connection is open. Their child spans arrive, so live traces lack the root and several parents.

I reproduced this with Codex sending directly to a local OTLP/HTTP JSON receiver, without a collector or tracing UI:

| Startup trace | Spans received | Root | Missing-parent references |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
| MCP connected, 4 seconds after startup | 164 | absent | 27 |
| 3 seconds after stopping only the mock MCP process | 174 | thread/start | 0 |

The Codex app-server stayed running throughout. This demonstrates delayed export, rather than permanent span loss.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use an isolated `CODEX_HOME` with one stdio MCP mock. It should answer `initialize` and `tools/list` (an empty tools list is sufficient), then keep the connection open. Use an unauthenticated local mock model provider; no turn needs to run.
2. Point tracing at a local HTTP receiver that records OTLP JSON requests and returns HTTP 200:

```toml
[otel]
exporter = "none"
metrics_exporter = "none"
trace_exporter = { otlp-http = { endpoint = "http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/traces", protocol = "json" } }
```

3. Start `codex app-server --stdio` with `OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY=200`. Send `initialize`, `initialized`, then `thread/start`. Wait several seconds and inspect the exported startup trace.
4. Stop only the mock MCP subprocess, leaving Codex running. The missing root and ancestor spans then arrive.

### What is the expected behavior?

Completed startup spans should be exported after startup finishes, independently of the lifetime of background MCP connections, so live traces have their root and parent spans.

### Additional information

Possible cause: the MCP initialization future uses [`.in_current_span()`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/4fd5745e8486d655a0c7e7d762741465b986130b/codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/rmcp_client.rs#L424), and rmcp 3.2.0 instruments its long-lived service task with the current span. This appears to retain the startup span ancestry until transport shutdown; tracing-opentelemetry exports on span close.

This is a source-level hypothesis, not a confirmed fix. The reproduction used the bundled version above; main at the linked commit was inspected, not rebuilt.

Thanks for taking a look!

items.body:
## What version of the Codex App are you using?
26.924.2738.0 (installed OpenAI.Codex Windows package checked September 28, 2026).

## What subscription do you have?
ChatGPT Pro ($200/month, user-reported).

## What platform is your computer?
Windows x64; OS reports Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0.

## What issue are you seeing?
**Delivered and already answered prompts remain as actionable queued items and block subsequent prompt delivery. This is an actual task-input/queue-state defect, not a feature request or a request to explain how queueing works.**

In the Work/task surface, I type a prompt in the Composer and press the send/up arrow. Intermittently, the prompt appears to enter the conversation, then immediately drops into the queue instead. The agent receives it and answers it, but the prompt remains in the queue while the answer is generated AND after the answer finishes. The user message is missing from its expected location in the transcript while its answer is already present.

I send my next prompt. It queues behind the stale, already-consumed prompt and does not reach the agent normally. Deleting the stale queue entry releases the next prompt, and the agent begins answering it. That next prompt can then repeat the same failure: it remains queued after being received and answered, blocking the following prompt.

The queue entry is still editable/deletable despite already having been consumed. Earlier occurrences in this workflow also showed deletion moving the already-answered prompt into its proper transcript position, and queue editing/deletion was associated with repeated delivery. The core report here is the reproducible user-observed sequence of stale consumed entries blocking subsequent input; the internal cause and duplicate-delivery mechanism are not independently established.

## What steps can reproduce the bug?
Intermittent sequence reported repeatedly by the user; not claimed to reproduce on every submission:
1. Open an existing Work-side task in the Windows Codex app.
2. Enter prompt A in the Composer and press the send/up arrow.
3. Observe A appear briefly as if entering the transcript, then remain as a queued item.
4. Observe the agent answer A and complete its response while A remains queued.
5. Enter prompt B and send it with the up arrow.
6. Observe B queue behind stale entry A rather than reach the agent normally.
7. Delete the already-answered A queue entry.
8. Observe B reach the agent and receive an answer, but potentially remain queued itself, repeating the blockage for prompt C.

Earlier screenshots provided to the reporting agent showed answered prompts still editable in the queue, including a Thank you followed by You're welcome with the Thank you still queued and absent from the transcript. The behavior was also observed after the queue menu indicated queueing was off. Those observations describe prior occurrences, not a controlled test of the setting.

## What is the expected behavior?
- A delivered/consumed prompt appears exactly once in the correct transcript position.
- Queue status reflects actual delivery state. An already consumed prompt cannot remain an actionable queue blocker after its response completes.
- Subsequent prompts flow normally without deleting earlier inputs.
- Delete/Edit has predictable semantics and does not cause accidental replay of an already-consumed prompt.
- Queue state, transcript state, and turn completion reconcile reliably, including with queueing disabled.

## Additional information / severity and requested engineering action
This is operationally disruptive and unacceptable. It makes an agent appear unresponsive while it has actually answered, obscures which prompt is being answered, blocks subsequent instructions, wastes working time, and forces the user to manipulate a misleading queue to continue ordinary conversation. It undermines confidence that steering instructions have been delivered. The workaround of deleting an already-answered message is not a fix and should not be required for basic prompt delivery.

Please triage this as a high-priority app bug, investigate synchronization between enqueue/delivery/consumption/transcript publication/turn completion, and test exactly-once delivery and forward progress when stale entries occur. Those are investigation areas, not an asserted diagnosis. Please provide an engineering owner/status and fix or reliable mitigation rather than generic queue-use guidance.

Related private support reports were submitted September 26 about stuck queues and delivered-versus-stale input visibility; no trackable case number was displayed. This issue supplies the explicit step-by-step failure sequence for a public engineering bug. It is separate from the chat-title renaming bug #45787.

Filed on behalf of Brent Reynolds with explicit authorization. No private transcript, account secrets, or unrelated project material is included.

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

Maintained Codex fork based on upstream commit 12de0e395d3313bc564190d983cb4f5acf0be713

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro — $200/month

### Which model were you using?

GPT-6 Astra Ultra

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 10 x64

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

_No response_

### Codex doctor report

```json

```

### What issue are you seeing?

## Summary

Codex prematurely triggered automatic compaction because its context estimator added **72,772 estimated tokens for prior encrypted reasoning** on top of a completed response's **177,413 reported tokens**.

The resulting count was **250,193 tokens**, crossing the **244,800 automatic-compaction threshold**, even though the last reported usage remained **67,387 tokens below that threshold**.

The incorrect threshold decision then caused a real additional remote compaction request consuming:

- **177,445 input tokens**
- **176,768 cached input tokens** (already included in input)
- **4,091 output tokens**
- **181,536 total reported tokens**

There was no manual compaction request.

## Exact calculation

Immediately before compaction:

| Measurement | Tokens |
| --- | ---: |
| Last response input | 176,904 |
| Cached input, included above | 173,952 |
| Last response output | 509 |
| Reasoning output, included above | 361 |
| **Last reported total** | **177,413** |
| Estimated earlier encrypted reasoning | **72,772** |
| Newly appended item estimate | **8** |
| **Count used for automatic compaction** | **250,193** |
| **Automatic-compaction threshold** | **244,800** |
| Effective context-window limit | **258,400** |

The decision was:

```text
177,413 + 72,772 + 8 = 250,193

250,193 >= 244,800  -> automatic compaction
250,193 < 258,400   -> full context-window limit not reached
```

Reconstructing the recorded history reproduces the **250,193-token count exactly**.

## Root cause

The additional **72,772 tokens** came from **148 encrypted reasoning items from earlier model responses** retained in history.

When `server_reasoning_included` is false, Codex effectively calculates:

```text
last reported total
+ estimated earlier reasoning
+ newly added items
```

The affected WebSocket handshake did not contain:

```text
X-Reasoning-Included
```

so this branch was used.

The defect is that **a historical subset is added to an already completed request's reported usage without establishing that the two quantities are disjoint**.

The 148 reasoning items were not newly generated reasoning. They matched the archived preceding request input by hash.

## Actual remote operation caused by the bug

| Operation | Input | Cached input | Output | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Response before compaction | 176,904 | 173,952 | 509 | 177,413 |
| **Automatic compaction** | **177,445** | **176,768** | **4,091** | **181,536** |
| First response afterward | 28,684 | 12,288 | 80 | 28,764 |

The compaction began immediately after the incorrect threshold decision.

This was not a UI-only accounting error. **The incorrect context calculation directly caused an additional remote model operation.**

## Upstream code

The running fork is based on upstream commit:

```text
12de0e395d3313bc564190d983cb4f5acf0be713
```

These functions were compared directly with that upstream commit and are unchanged:

```text
codex-rs/core/src/context_manager/history.rs

get_non_last_reasoning_items_tokens
get_total_token_usage
is_user_turn_boundary
```

Relevant upstream code:

```text
core/src/context_manager/history.rs
    prior-reasoning estimate and total-token calculation

core/src/state/session.rs
    server_reasoning_included state and history accounting

core/src/session/context_window.rs
    automatic-compaction threshold comparison

core/src/session/turn.rs
    server flag handling and compaction decision

codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs
    X-Reasoning-Included handling

codex-api/src/endpoint/responses_websocket.rs
    corresponding WebSocket handling
```

## Correct accounting

For a settled request with a complete request-bound estimate, the context baseline should compare complete quantities rather than add historical reasoning to an already completed total:

```text
baseline = max(
    last server-reported input + output,
    estimated complete composed input + actual output
)

next context estimate =
    baseline + genuinely new local-item estimate
```

For this incident:

```text
archived complete-input estimate: 201,228
developer-message normalization:    -990
inserted text upper bound:          +2,812
                                     -------
complete composed-input bound:     203,050
```

Therefore:

```text
max(177,413, 203,050 + 509) + 8
= 203,567

203,567 < 244,800
```

The correct decision does **not** trigger automatic compaction.

## Related open issues

This sits within a much larger existing set of open Codex usage/accounting defects:

- [#41220 — Abnormal Codex usage/quota depletion and usage-accounting inconsistencies — cross-report tracker](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/41220)
- [#47825 — Hosted search usage causes premature auto-compaction](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/47825)
- [#47003 — Auto-compaction request usage is never added to `total_token_usage`](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/47003)
- [#45074 — Automatic compaction at 388K displayed tokens uses a 623K internal count](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/45074)
- [#48919 — 36,318-token request followed by ~6% 5-hour depletion and ~2.95M daily tokens](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48919)
- [#46681 — Weekly usage dropped from ~75% to 16% in 19 minutes despite 98,700 reported tokens](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/46681)
- [#44386 — ~150K cached input replayed per tool call, rapidly draining usage](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/44386)
- [#38495 — Full-context polling loop consumed 34.6M tokens after work had completed](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/38495)
- [#35463 — Subagent history/accounting behavior associated with an entire weekly quota drain](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/35463)
- [#32640 — Repeated wait/resampling behavior causing massive token consumption](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/32640)

## Customer impact

I pay **$200/month for ChatGPT Pro**, and I now maintain both my own Codex fork and an increasingly substantial local instrumentation and patching layer around it.

I find the current situation completely absurd: **I am spending a meaningful portion of my paid OpenAI allowance using OpenAI's own models to identify, diagnose, and patch defects in OpenAI's own Codex client that themselves waste that allowance.**

This bug is a concrete example. An incorrect client-side accounting decision caused an additional **181,536-token remote operation that should not have occurred at that point**.

This is also not an isolated class of problem. The issue tracker already contains a substantial number of open reports involving incorrect accounting, unnecessary context replay, runaway polling, premature compaction, background activity, and subscription usage that does not reconcile with observable work.

A normal client bug wastes time.

**A client bug that causes unnecessary inference consumes the product the customer paid for.**

At $200/month, I should not have to spend an increasing portion of that same finite allowance maintaining a private patch layer around the official client simply to prevent avoidable usage consumption.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use a Codex session containing retained encrypted reasoning items from earlier model responses.

2. Reach a completed response where the server-reported token total remains below the automatic-compaction threshold.

3. Have `server_reasoning_included == false`, as occurs when the response does not contain `X-Reasoning-Included`.

4. Append a new history item after that completed response.

5. Allow the normal Codex history-accounting path to evaluate the automatic-compaction threshold.

In the captured incident:

new-item estimate:                       8

automatic-compaction threshold:    244,800
context-window limit:              258,400

output_tokens:           4,091

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.917.71314

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Business

### What platform is your computer?

Linux 7.0.0-34-generic x86_64

### What issue are you seeing?

When working in a long Codex conversation, the active Goal can sometimes be lost after automatic context compaction.
For example, I may work in the same conversation for about an hour and solve problems X and Y. I then encounter a more complex problem Z, so I start a new Goal specifically for Z and explain what needs to be done.
Codex initially behaves correctly: it starts the Goal, scans the relevant files, and begins working on problem Z. However, after the message indicating that the context was automatically compacted appears, Codex can lose track of the active Goal and return to an older problem from earlier in the conversation, such as problem Y, even though that problem has already been completed.
As a result, Codex may start working on previously completed tasks instead of continuing with the currently active Goal.
I have encountered this behavior multiple times recently.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1 - Work in the same Codex conversation for an extended period of time.
2 - Complete several tasks/problems in that conversation (for example, problems X and Y).
3 - Start a new Goal for a different and more complex problem (problem Z).
4 - Let Codex work on the Goal until automatic context compaction occurs.
5 - After the context is compacted, Codex may lose track of problem Z and resume working on one of the previously completed problems.

### What is the expected behavior?

The currently active Goal should remain the primary objective even after automatic context compaction.
Context compaction should preserve the active Goal and its current progress. Previously completed tasks from earlier in the conversation should not become active again unless they are explicitly relevant to the current Goal.

### Additional information

This seems specifically related to automatic context compaction rather than the initial Goal creation. The Goal starts correctly and Codex initially understands the task, but the loss of focus happens after the context is compacted.

items.body:
## Summary

In ChatGPT for Android, Codex Remote is slow to open an existing thread and to switch between threads on the **same Windows host**, even after the host has connected and the thread list is visible. Going back to a thread I just viewed triggers another noticeable loading wait. The threads eventually open, but this repeated delay makes ordinary navigation cumbersome.

This focuses on **thread navigation after host connection**. #29201 reports slow reconnects when entering Remote or switching hosts; I also experience that delay, but switching threads on one already selected host adds a separate wait.

## Environment

- ChatGPT for Android: `1.2026.265` (version code `2626523`)
- Android 16; device model `V2417A`
- Codex Desktop for Windows: `26.924.2738.0`
- Windows 11 Pro x64, build `22631`
- Phone and host are on the same Wi-Fi network. This does **not** establish that Remote traffic uses a direct LAN connection.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In ChatGPT for Android, open Codex Remote and select the Windows host.
2. Wait for the host to connect and for its thread list to appear.
3. Open an existing thread and wait for its conversation/history to appear.
4. Return to the thread list and open another existing thread.
5. Return to the first thread, then repeat the switch.

## Actual behavior

- Opening each thread takes a noticeable loading wait, including a thread opened moments earlier.
- Switching threads repeatedly incurs the same sort of wait instead of feeling like immediate navigation within an already connected host.
- Entering Remote and showing the connected host also takes a noticeable wait.
- I have not captured controlled timings, so I am not claiming a specific number of seconds or a measured regression.
- I cannot tell from the UI whether the delay is caused by transport reconnection, host-side `thread/list` / `thread/resume`, history transfer, or Android rendering.

## Expected behavior

Once a host and thread list are available, opening another thread or returning to a recently viewed thread should become usable promptly. If loading older history is expensive, show the latest messages and composer first and load older history progressively. A visible status or actionable error would help distinguish a slow load from a failed connection.

## Related reports and diagnostics

- #29201: repeated slow reconnects on Android when entering Remote or switching hosts.
- #25495: slow Remote Control reconnection.
- #45246: a separately measured `thread/list` delay on a host with many unarchived threads. I have **not** established that its root cause applies here.
- #47148: a large conversation that remains stuck loading; my report concerns repeated waits while switching threads that eventually open.

Another remote coding app feels substantially quicker to navigate on the same phone and Wi-Fi, but this is only a user-experience comparison, not a controlled network or implementation benchmark.

Please investigate and, if possible, expose separate timings for host connection, thread listing, thread resume/history retrieval, and mobile rendering. I can provide sanitized diagnostics if the team specifies what would be most useful; raw session logs may contain private conversation contents and are not attached here.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

codex-cli 0.144.0

### What subscription do you have?

Team

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm

### What issue are you seeing?

Every tool invocation through functions.exec fails while decoding the
  code-mode IPC response. The response contains a field named
  code_mode_host_duration_ns, but the consumer schema rejects that field.

  This prevents the assistant from receiving stdout, stderr, exit codes, or
  results from local and web tools.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

 1. Start a Codex session with tool execution enabled.
  2. Invoke a minimal command through functions.exec:

     const result = await tools.exec_command({ cmd: "pwd" });
     text(result.output);

  3. Observe that no command result is returned.
  4. Repeat with another tool or command. The same decoding error occurs.

  The issue reproduced with pwd, codex --version, rg, sed, brew upgrade, and
  web-tool calls.



### What is the expected behavior?

  ### Expected behavior

  functions.exec should decode the tool-host response and return the command's
  stdout, stderr, exit code, or running-session identifier. Optional telemetry
  fields should not prevent the response from being decoded.

  ### Actual behavior

  The IPC decoder rejects code_mode_host_duration_ns as an unknown field, and
  the entire tool call fails. No usable result reaches the assistant.

  ### Error/log output

  failed to read code-mode host message: failed to decode code-mode IPC frame:
  unknown field `code_mode_host_duration_ns`, expected one of
  `cell_id`, `content_items`, `error_text`

  Also include the variant encountered during the escalated operation:

  failed to read code-mode host message: failed to decode code-mode IPC frame:
  unknown field `code_mode_host_duration_ns`, expected `cell_id` or
  `content_items`

  ### Frequency

  Always — reproduced on every functions.exec call in the affected session.

  ### Regression

  Unknown. I do not know which previously installed version last worked.
  The installed Homebrew cask is currently up to date.

  ### Impact/severity

  High for the affected session. All assistant tool execution is blocked,
  including basic shell commands and web-tool calls. Conversational responses
  still work.

  ### Model

  Appears model-independent. The failure occurs at the tool-host IPC decoding
  boundary before a usable tool result reaches the assistant.

### Additional information

  This appears to be a producer/consumer schema-version mismatch. The producer
  emits code_mode_host_duration_ns, while the consumer rejects unknown fields.

  A likely compatibility fix is to add the field as optional:

  #[serde(default)]
  code_mode_host_duration_ns: Option<u64>

  Alternatively, the IPC envelope decoder could tolerate unknown optional
  telemetry fields. Responses both with and without this field should be covered
  by compatibility tests.

  Because the response could not be decoded, I cannot determine reliably
  whether the nested commands executed before the decoding failure.

## Summary

Two macOS Codex desktop managed worktrees remain registered in Git, but their owning tasks expose no worktree attachment through `list_artifacts`. The supported `archive_worktree` operation requires the exact `identityKey`/`root` from that attachment, so these completed reviewer checkouts cannot be archived safely.

## Affected tasks

- Task `01a0e51a-8262-7221-9dbe-39297392f1d4`: active, idle reviewer chat; checkout suffix `$CODEX_HOME/worktrees/8904/mobile_scanner_b2m`; Git reports detached HEAD `ec836777ac026e9a1cb2dce6dde1bdaaae2fd5ac`. Its `list_artifacts` returns an attached PR but no worktree identity.
- Task `01a0e4c0-1375-74b2-a66f-a4453c9b1a26`: archived reviewer chat; checkout suffix `$CODEX_HOME/worktrees/c0e9/mobile_scanner_b2m`; Git reports detached HEAD `0b06bdae41c0bdfab740daaf95e1e5f412e81a64`. Its last `list_artifacts` check likewise returned no worktree identity. Archiving the chat did not remove the Git registration.

Both checkouts contain ignored local material. We have preserved it and have not run shell deletion, `git worktree remove`, or `git worktree prune`. The 8904 tracked checkout is clean; process absence could not be established by the available guarded check. We have not exposed ignored-file contents, credentials, or local logs in this report.

## Expected behavior and request

Please restore each existing task's managed-worktree attachment so `archive_worktree` can target that exact checkout, or provide a supported orphan-worktree archive route that first preserves ignored files and checks process ownership. The route should let us verify both filesystem path removal and Git worktree deregistration before closing the associated cleanup issues.

## Observed behavior

The app tool catalog has `list_artifacts`, `archive_worktree`, and `restore_worktree`, but no control to attach an existing checkout to its task. `archive_worktree` accepts only an identity returned by the calling task's `list_artifacts`. Guessing a root or archiving the chat alone is not safe for these checkouts.

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.158.0` (`rust-v0.158.0`, the latest stable GitHub release when checked on 2026-09-28).

### What subscription do you have?

Not applicable to this reproduction: local mock Responses provider with dummy credentials; no hosted model or subscription used.

### Which model were you using?

A local fixture returns one completed assistant message (`ok`). No model inference is involved.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 26.5.1 (25F80), Apple Silicon. `uname -mprs`: `Darwin 25.5.0 arm64 arm`.

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Non-interactive `codex exec`, launched as a subprocess with stdin closed and stdout/stderr redirected to files. No TUI or multiplexer involved in the reproduction.

### What issue are you seeing?

`codex exec` intermittently exits with status 0 without completing a synchronous `SessionEnd` hook whose entire command is a shell builtin writing a marker file. The corresponding `SessionStart` marker exists, and the model turn completes successfully.

The failure still occurs with `notify = []` and all three native OTEL exporters disabled. There are no external hook handlers, MCP servers, plugins, or network operations in the hooks.

Native process sampling and source inspection point to synchronous macOS filesystem-watcher teardown consuming the in-process app-server's five-second shutdown budget before core session teardown reaches the end hook. The blocking operation is observed; the full cancellation/lifetime mechanism below is a source-based diagnosis, not yet validated with a patched Codex build.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Save the standalone Python script below as `repro.py`, then run:

```sh
python3 repro.py 10 /path/to/codex
```

Requirements: Python 3, Git, Codex 0.158.0, macOS. It starts a loopback HTTP fixture and creates a fresh temporary repository, HOME, and CODEX_HOME for every iteration. It does not use or modify the normal Codex profile. It retains temporary artifacts and prints their location. Exit code 1 means a missing end marker; 2 means an invalid run.

Hook trust is explicitly bypassed only for these scratch marker hooks with `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust`; the shell sandbox remains `workspace-write`. The failure is intermittent and may depend on system FSEvents state, so a passing batch does not rule it out.

<details>
<summary>Standalone reproducer (Python standard library)</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Local-only Codex SessionEnd probe. Usage: python3 repro.py [runs] [codex]"""
import http.server
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading

class Provider(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass

    def do_POST(self):
        self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get('Content-Length', 0)))
        item = {'type': 'message', 'id': 'msg_probe', 'role': 'assistant',
                'status': 'completed', 'content': [
                    {'type': 'output_text', 'text': 'ok', 'annotations': []}]}
        response = {'id': 'resp_probe', 'object': 'response',
                    'status': 'completed', 'output': [item],
                    'usage': {'input_tokens': 12, 'output_tokens': 4,
                              'total_tokens': 16}}
        events = [
            ('response.created', {'response': dict(response, status='in_progress', output=[])}),
            ('response.output_item.added', {'output_index': 0, 'item': item}),
            ('response.output_item.done', {'output_index': 0, 'item': item}),
            ('response.completed', {'response': response}),
        ]
        data = ''.join('event: ' + name + '\ndata: ' +
                       json.dumps(dict(payload, type=name)) + '\n\n'
                       for name, payload in events).encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header('Content-Type', 'text/event-stream')
        self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(data)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

runs = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 10
binary = shutil.which(sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 'codex')
if not binary:
    sys.exit('Codex executable not found')
root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='codex-session-end-')).resolve()
print('Artifacts:', root, flush=True)
print(subprocess.check_output([binary, '--version'], text=True).strip(), flush=True)
server = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', 0), Provider)
threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
missing = invalid = 0
try:
    for n in range(1, runs + 1):
        base = root / str(n)
        repo, home, config = base / 'repo', base / 'home', base / 'codex'
        for p in (repo / '.codex', home, config):
            p.mkdir(parents=True)
        env = {'PATH': '/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin',
               'HOME': str(home), 'CODEX_HOME': str(config), 'TERM': 'xterm-256color',
               'OPENAI_API_KEY': 'dummy-local-fixture-key',
               'RUST_LOG': 'codex_core=debug,codex_app_server=debug,codex_hooks=trace'}
        subprocess.run(['git', 'init', '-q', str(repo)], env=env, check=True)
        (config / 'config.toml').write_text('''
cli_auth_credentials_store = "file"
notify = []
model_provider = "local_fixture"
model_reasoning_effort = "low"
[features]
hooks = true
plugins = false
remote_plugin = false
[otel]
exporter = "none"
trace_exporter = "none"
metrics_exporter = "none"
[model_providers.local_fixture]
name = "Local fixture"
wire_api = "responses"
requires_openai_auth = false
base_url = "http://127.0.0.1:PORT"
'''.replace('PORT', str(server.server_port)) +
            '\n[projects.' + json.dumps(str(repo)) + ']\ntrust_level = "trusted"\n')
        (config / 'auth.json').write_text(json.dumps({'OPENAI_API_KEY': 'dummy-local-fixture-key'}))
        hooks = {'hooks': {event: [{'hooks': [{
            'type': 'command', 'command': 'printf ' + marker + ' > .codex/probe-' + marker,
            'timeout': 3}]}] for event, marker in
            [('SessionStart', 'start'), ('SessionEnd', 'end')]}}
        (repo / '.codex/hooks.json').write_text(json.dumps(hooks))
        args = [binary, 'exec', '--json', '--skip-git-repo-check',
                '--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust', '-s', 'workspace-write',
                '-C', str(repo), 'Reply briefly.']
        with (base / 'stdout.log').open('w') as out, (base / 'stderr.log').open('w') as err:
            result = subprocess.run(args, cwd=repo, env=env, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
                                    stdout=out, stderr=err, timeout=90)
        started = (repo / '.codex/probe-start').exists()
        ended = (repo / '.codex/probe-end').exists()
        print(f'{n}: exit={result.returncode} SessionStart={started} SessionEnd={ended}', flush=True)
        if result.returncode != 0 or not started:
            invalid += 1
        elif not ended:
            missing += 1
finally:
    server.shutdown()
print(f'Missing SessionEnd: {missing}/{runs}; invalid runs: {invalid}', flush=True)
sys.exit(2 if invalid else 1 if missing else 0)
```

</details>

### What is the expected behavior?

A normal successful `codex exec` shutdown should allow the configured synchronous `SessionEnd` hook to execute within its own bounded timeout. A fast marker hook should not be silently lost because unrelated watcher cleanup consumed the shutdown budget. If shutdown cannot satisfy that lifecycle contract, expose a clear diagnostic.

### Additional information

#### Measured results

The standalone script above was run on 2026-09-28: **3/10 runs missed `SessionEnd`**, with **0 invalid runs**. All ten exited with status 0 and wrote the `SessionStart` marker. No process sampler was running during this batch.

| Run | Listener-clear log → core `Op::Shutdown` | End marker |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1.02 s | Present |
| 2 | 5.48 s | Missing |
| 3 | 1.29 s | Present |
| 4 | 0.12 s | Present |
| 5 | 2.06 s | Present |
| 6 | 1.74 s | Present |
| 7 | 2.76 s | Present |
| 8 | 5.48 s | Missing |
| 9 | 5.48 s | Missing |
| 10 | 3.83 s | Present |

An earlier independent marker-only control with notifier and exporters disabled also missed the hook in 2/10 runs. In those failures, the gap between `clearing thread listener during app-server shutdown` and core receiving `Op::Shutdown` was 7.65 seconds and 5.56 seconds. One failure happened before process sampling began.

During the 5.56-second failure, a one-second native sample captured the shutdown worker blocked in:

```text
codex_app_server::thread_state::ThreadState::clear_listener
  <codex_file_watcher::WatchRegistration as Drop>::drop
    [stripped frames]
      _dispatch_semaphore_wait_slow
        semaphore_wait_trap
```

At the same time, the `notify-rs fsevents loop` thread was blocked in:

```text
FSEventStreamStart
  register_with_server
    f2d_register_rpc
      mach_msg2_trap
```

Both stacks persisted across all 818 samples of those threads in that interval. These excerpts omit local paths, binary-image listings and unrelated process data.

#### Source-based diagnosis (pinned to the tested release)

1. [`ThreadState::clear_listener`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.158.0/codex-rs/app-server/src/thread_state.rs#L145) replaces `self.watch_registration`, synchronously dropping the previous registration.
2. [`WatchRegistration::drop`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.158.0/codex-rs/file-watcher/src/lib.rs#L362) unregisters paths. [`reconfigure_watch_inner`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.158.0/codex-rs/file-watcher/src/lib.rs#L564) calls the native watcher's `unwatch`/`watch` operations. The sample locates the wait in this path.
3. The [processor cleanup sequence](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.158.0/codex-rs/app-server/src/in_process.rs#L591) clears listeners, drains background tasks, then shuts down threads. The [outer shutdown timeout](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.158.0/codex-rs/app-server/src/in_process.rs#L793) aborts the processor after five seconds. A synchronous blocking destructor cannot be preempted by an async timeout.
4. [Background draining and thread shutdown](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.158.0/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L1267) each allow ten seconds, exceeding that outer budget.
5. [`run_session_end_hooks`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.158.0/codex-rs/core/src/session/handlers.rs#L287) runs late in core shutdown. Its [three-second maximum](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.158.0/codex-rs/hooks/src/events/session_end.rs#L20) leaves nominal headroom within the five-second outer bound, but does not reserve time against preceding cleanup.

Suggested direction: remove blocking watch reconfiguration from the async shutdown critical path, make nested deadlines consistent, and preserve a bounded opportunity for session-end hooks before tearing down the runtime. A regression test could deliberately block watcher cleanup and verify that the marker hook still completes; another should cover a hanging hook and bounded shutdown. Merely increasing the outer timeout would leave hook delivery dependent on native cleanup latency.

#### Related reports

- #43377: missing `SessionEnd` on Windows Desktop quit; different platform and apparent shutdown mechanism.
- #38783: macOS startup/quit stalls; its attached native sample also includes `clear_listener → WatchRegistration::drop`, though the report focuses on TLS and does not establish missing end hooks.
- #34376: multi-second macOS FSEvents teardown stalls in the Electron UI, a different caller.
- #44610: request to disable filesystem watchers for headless `codex exec` runs.

I could not find an existing report connecting this macOS CLI watcher teardown path to omitted `SessionEnd` hooks.
